commit.message:
Implement the import feature: read live agents back into the folder

Adds `agentlift import` — the inverse of `deploy`. A reverse pipeline
reconstructs a neutral .managed-agents/ folder from a live runtime, so a
runtime now round-trips both ways and migration between runtimes falls out
for free (import from one provider, deploy to another).

New modules (pure core + thin network edge, mirroring the deploy pipeline):
- import_model.py        ImportedProject/Agent/Skill/Mcp dataclasses
- importer.py            raw provider dicts -> ImportedProject (inverse of planner):
                         tool decode, Bedrock model reverse-map, roster id->name,
                         shared-resource hoisting (skills by content hash, MCP by identity)
- folder_writer.py       ImportedProject -> .managed-agents/ files (inverse of parser)
- anthropic_source.py    live Anthropic -> raw dicts (list/retrieve + skill download,
                         roster closure, zip unpack re-prefixed to the skill name)
- harness_source.py      live Bedrock harness -> raw dict (get_harness + S3 skills)

CLI: `import <anthropic|bedrock> <out> [--agent N ...] [--mode harness]
[--harness-id|--harness-name] [--bedrock-region R] [--dry-run]`. Read-only;
self-verifies by re-running the real parse+plan ("Round-trip OK"). A Bedrock
runtime is an opaque container -> `--mode runtime` refuses.

Anthropic import is full (tools+policies, URL MCP+filters, custom skill content,
coordinator subagents). Bedrock harness import covers config + S3 skills with a
reverse model-map. One-way losses (knowledge inlining, custom tools, MCP auth
values, first-party skills) are each surfaced as a diagnostic, never silent.

Tests: test_importer (mapping contract), test_import_roundtrip (provider ->
folder -> real parser -> real planner, incl. subagent delegation with shared AND
custom skills and MCP servers), test_import_source (fetch wiring via fake
clients), test_cli_import, and a gated read-only live test. Full suite green
(328 passed). Regression tests added for review findings (skill name/arcname
normalization; same-content/different-name hoisting).

Docs: new docs/import.md; import notes across CLAUDE.md, README.md, and the
convention/how-it-works/provider-matrix/anthropic-mapping/deploy-bedrock/
deploying/limitations docs; CHANGELOG drafted under [Unreleased] (not released).

commit.message:
release: 0.7.0 — live AgentCore Runtime (Stage 2)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

bedrock Stage 2: live multi-agent AgentCore Runtime hosted deploy

The custom-container Runtime primitive is now a LIVE hosted deploy (was
build-only). `--mode runtime` builds an ARM64 container, pushes to ECR, calls
CreateAgentRuntime (PUBLIC/HTTP/IAM-only), polls READY, writes
.agentlift-bedrock.json, and InvokeAgentRuntime. Gated by _RUNTIME_LIVE_VERIFIED
(now True) — a bare hosted create refused until a committed receipt.

Live-verified on Nova (us-east-1), two committed receipts:
- team (20260605-134012): create + agent + subagent DELEGATION all
  PASS-EXERCISED (coordinator top-level tool_calls = ['bug_finder','researcher']);
  nested skill/MCP PASS-WIRED (text-corroborated).
- smoke (20260605-133821): create + agent + remote_mcp PASS-EXERCISED (objective
  root-level docs_read_wiki_structure DeepWiki call).

Honest /invocations boundary: InvokeAgentRuntime returns the container's JSON body,
not an event stream. The generated handler returns {result, tool_calls?} where
tool_calls is the coordinator's top-level trace (AgentResult.metrics.tool_metrics,
fail-open). Delegation + root-level tools are objective; nested specialist
skill/MCP calls don't cross the boundary (the Google AgentTool→stream_query
analogue).

- bedrock_target: hosted-create path (ECR repo+login+buildx push + CreateAgentRuntime
  + poll + lock + InvokeAgentRuntime), seam-injected for offline tests; gate backstop.
- bedrock_codegen: defensive top-level tool-call trace capture in the handler.
- bedrock_plan/lock: _RUNTIME_LIVE_VERIFIED flag + runtime_hosted_deploy_allowed();
  lock now live-writing.
- tests/live/runtime.py verifier + runtime-single/runtime-team fixtures.
- offline tests: test_bedrock_hosted, test_live_runtime_orchestration,
  test_runtime_receipt (293 offline green).
- docs: README/CLAUDE/docs reconciled — Runtime live, Claude-native mapping with
  Nova wire-shape receipts (Claude inference Gate-A-gated, not a code gap), the
  /invocations boundary, and the MCP per-tool-filter limitation narrowed to the
  direct remote_mcp path (Gateway+Policy enforces server-side; not yet verified).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix CI: declare boto3 as the `bedrock` extra; install it in CI

The 0.6.0 AWS Bedrock target uses boto3 (live harness create/invoke + skill S3
upload), but boto3 was never a declared dependency — so CI (`.[dev,google]`) ran
without it and `test_live_harness_orchestration.py` (which patches boto3.client)
errored on main.

- pyproject: add `bedrock = ["boto3>=1.43"]` optional extra (parallels `google`);
  live `--target bedrock` deploy needs it (audit/plan/export stay offline-only)
- ci.yml: install `.[dev,google,bedrock]` (offline) and `.[dev,bedrock]` (live)
- test_live_harness_orchestration.py: `pytest.importorskip("boto3")` so a lean
  `.[dev]` install skips it cleanly instead of erroring
- docs/deploy-bedrock.md: `pip install "agentlift[bedrock]"` in the setup

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

AWS Bedrock AgentCore Harness: live single-agent deploy (0.6.0)

Deploy one neutral folder live to a managed AgentCore Harness — agent + skills
+ remote MCP + base-session sandbox + browser — config-only, IAM-only, no
container. Claude-native, no model remap. `--mode auto` routes a single agent
to the Harness and a multi-agent team to the build-only Runtime, never a silent
downgrade.

Live-verified 6/6 by a committed Nova receipt
(tests/live/receipts/20260605-121525-harness-bedrock): CreateHarness -> READY,
then InvokeHarness exercised agent + sandbox (shell) + remote MCP
(docs_read_wiki_structure, surfaced as <server>_<tool>) + an S3-loaded skill
(skills[].s3.uri) + agentcore_browser, all server-side.

- harness_plan/lock/target.py: pure plan + boto3 create/invoke/get/delete; skills
  upload to $AGENTLIFT_BEDROCK_S3_BUCKET; clientToken-deleted retry; CLI --mode
- Runtime (--mode runtime --build-only): ARM64 container build-only; hosted
  multi-agent create is a fast-follow
- docs reconciled (README restructure ~494->214, provider-matrix, deploy-bedrock,
  tested-platforms, CLAUDE, limitations); CHANGELOG; doc-link CI guard
- also in this release: Google built-in web tools, Claude-on-Vertex offline spike
- version 0.6.0; 274 offline tests green; AWS account id anonymized in the receipt

Honest caveats: the AgentCore Harness feature is in AWS public preview; Claude
inference is Gate-A-gated (the Nova receipt is model-agnostic for the wire shape);
per-tool MCP allowlist narrowing is not enforced on the harness preview.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add AWS Bedrock AgentCore deploy target (build-only preview)

agentlift's fourth runtime target: compile the neutral .managed-agents/
folder to a deployable AWS Bedrock AgentCore Runtime container.

Pipeline mirrors the Anthropic/Google discipline (plan is the contract):
- bedrock_plan.py   (pure)  Project -> BedrockDeployPlan: Strands recipe,
                            agents-as-tools subagents, skills, URL MCP +
                            tool_filter, inline-auth env-var names, native
                            Claude model map (region prefix -> regional
                            inference profile, NO Gemini-style remap), spec
                            hash, diagnostics.
- bedrock_codegen.py (pure) plan -> source package: agentlift_runtime/agent.py
                            + requirements + ARM64 Dockerfile + .dockerignore
                            + NOTES.txt runbook + embedded SKILL.md bundles.
- bedrock_lock.py   (pure)  .agentlift-bedrock.json spec-hash state +
                            decide_action -> create/update/skip.
- bedrock_target.py (net)   --build-only materializes the full ARM64 build
                            context under .agentlift-build/bedrock/; a bare
                            hosted `deploy --target bedrock` REFUSES (the
                            AgentCore control-plane create wire shape is not
                            live-verified here — confirm-live-before-encoding).

export target `bedrock-strands` emits the same Strands scaffold offline.
capabilities.py gains the bedrock column; audit/export read it as the single
source of truth. CLI wires plan/audit/export/deploy --target bedrock.

Honesty framing (two axes kept distinct, double-checked with Codex):
- audit/capabilities rate the PLATFORM (AgentCore hosted_runtime = native).
- the maturity table rates agentlift's SHIPPED implementation (BUILD-ONLY
  PREVIEW — refuses the unverified hosted-create).
- Claude-native is stated strictly as a MAPPING fact (compiler emits the
  Bedrock Claude inference-profile id directly, no remap), NOT proven
  inference. The live same-Claude composition receipt is PENDING Gate A
  (the per-account Anthropic use-case form, eventually consistent — it
  flapped to BEDROCK_OK once then back to ResourceNotFoundException). The
  Strands composition itself is live-proven on Amazon Nova Pro.

Two one-time gates documented (both outside the code path): Gate A = the
Anthropic use-case entitlement; Gate B = AWS IAM creds + execution role +
ECR for the hosted create.

Docs: new docs/deploy-bedrock.md; README + CLAUDE.md + provider-matrix.md +
tested-platforms.md + limitations.md reframed to present the runtimes in
Anthropic / AWS / Google / OpenAI order (AWS second). experiments/
bedrock-composition/ carries the live Nova-Pro composition proof + the
Gate A flapping write-up.

Offline suite: 182 passed (parse/plan/codegen pure, every translation rule
has an offline test). Only bedrock_target.py touches the network.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Google web tools (web_search/web_fetch) + CI-safe offline exec tests

Implements the built-in web tools for the Google target (--target google),
live-verified, and fixes the red CI on main.

Feature: web_search and web_fetch now map to Google instead of being skipped.
- web_search -> Gemini's Google Search grounding; web_fetch -> URL Context.
- Each is lowered as a dedicated single-tool ADK sub-agent wrapped in an
  AgentTool (propagate_grounding_metadata=True), so the web tools coexist with
  MCP toolsets, skills, and transfer_to_agent on the same agent. Always-wrap:
  transfer tools are injected at request time and not counted by len(self.tools),
  so we cannot conditionally skip the wrapper.
- An agent with no `tools:` frontmatter (all built-ins) gets BOTH web tools.
- capabilities.py splits the old `builtin_tools` feature into `builtin_web`
  (now emulated/mapped on Google) and `builtin_sandbox` (still degraded/skipped,
  Vertex's sandbox is Python/JS only). audit + export read the split.
- google-adk>=1.34.3 is pinned in the deployed requirements whenever any web
  tool is present (the version the wrapper path was verified on).

Live verification: a dedicated web-tools fixture was deployed to a real
reasoningEngine and queried; both wrapped tool-agents fired server-side
(function_call + function_response), and web_fetch returned a unique nonce
canary verbatim. Receipt: tests/live/receipts/20260604-115352-web-google
(Google identifiers anonymized; engine torn down after the run).

CI fix: the offline exec tests build a real Vertex AdkApp, whose constructor
eagerly reads initializer.global_config.project and resolves Application
Default Credentials -- which fails on CI (no ADC). This is what turned main red
at the 0.5.0 release. New `offline_vertex` fixture pins a fake project +
AnonymousCredentials via vertexai.init, then booby-traps google.auth.default to
prove the construction path resolves no ADC, and snapshots/restores the Vertex
global config so the fake project doesn't leak. Full offline suite is green
under a simulated no-ADC environment (empty CLOUDSDK_CONFIG + cleared GOOGLE_*).

Docs: README, provider-matrix, limitations, tested-platforms, deploy-google,
demo/README, and CLAUDE.md updated for the web-tools mapping and the
sandbox/web split. AGENTS.md is now a pure pointer to CLAUDE.md (single source
of truth for Claude and Codex). CLAUDE.md gains a prominent mandatory rule:
anonymize Google project IDs / resource names / bucket / project number before
every commit.

skylift v0.1.0 — deploy local Claude agents to Anthropic Managed Agents

A deterministic translator + deployer: point it at the agent folder you
already use locally (.agents/ or the Claude Code .claude/agents/ layout) and
it uploads skills, maps the tool allowlist, wires remote MCP servers, folds in
knowledge files, and creates the hosted agent by ID.

Core (parse -> plan -> apply -> run):
- parser: .agents/ + .claude/agents back-compat, shared skills/MCP, frontmatter
- planner: pure, deterministic plan with symbolic refs; skill dedup by content
  hash; stdio-MCP rejection; tool/MCP/multiagent mapping; limit validation
- anthropic_target: skill upload (content-addressed titles), agent create in
  dependency order, idempotent lockfile
- runtime: managed session streaming + a local runner (same folder, two runtimes)
- cost, graders (substring + LLM), CLI (validate/plan/deploy/run/list/destroy/bench)

Verified live against the real API (2026-06-02): skill upload + apply in-cloud,
tool allowlist, URL MCP, multiagent coordinator all confirmed. 15 offline tests
+ 2 live LLM-graded tests pass. Benchmark: 100% pass on managed and local.
